decision.summary: Conditional approval of Outdoor Solar PTZ Camera concept pending quantification of solar energy budget inputs, pan-scope selection, and zoom-in-wind stability limits.
decision.recommendation: Proceed with the core dual-chip architecture (Sigmastar SSC338Q SoC for video/AI + STM32G431 MCU for motor control), event-triggered streaming, and pan-limits design. Do not commit or freeze the spec until the solar panel Wp, deployment sun-hours, battery Wh, and autonomy days are provided to close the energy budget, and maximum zoom ratio is capped via wind-resonance testing.

assumptions.statement: Daily consumption is standby-dominated (~7.2 Wh/day at ~0.3 W standby) and total daily energy consumption can be kept within ~8-12 Wh/day using event-triggered streaming.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: If standby or active duty power exceeds harvest, the system will experience battery depletion and shutdown.

assumptions.statement: Pan limits (e.g. ±180° or ±270° with unwind) will be selected instead of true endless 360° rotation.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Selecting endless pan forces a slip ring, introducing electromechanical wear, contact resistance, and severe IP66 sealing complexity.

assumptions.statement: IMU-driven EIS combined with a stiff low-clamp mount can stabilize optical zoom video under light to moderate wind.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Unmitigated low-frequency umbrella sway will produce shaky, unusable zoomed video in outdoor breeze.

assumptions.statement: Self-locking gearing (worm drive or detent) or balanced camera head geometry eliminates continuous stepper holding current when static.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Continuous motor holding current will drain the battery rapidly, breaking the daily energy budget.

assumptions.statement: Battery charging will be hardware-inhibited below 0 °C or chemistry will be switched to LiFePO4.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Charging standard Li-ion cells below freezing causes lithium plating, severe capacity degradation, and safety risks.

risks.description: Solar energy budget fails to close due to unquantified panel Wp, umbrella shading, and low seasonal sun-hours.
risks.mitigation: Require engineer to provide panel Wp, deployment latitude/sun-hours, battery Wh, and autonomy days; enforce strict event-driven streaming and adaptive duty cycle.

risks.description: Optical zoom magnifies umbrella mount sway under wind loading, yielding unusable video.
risks.mitigation: Clamp mount low on rigid pole section, minimize head mass and moment arm, implement IMU-assisted EIS, and cap maximum optical zoom ratio.

risks.description: Open-loop stepper skips steps under wind gusts or physical obstruction, causing PTZ preset position drift.
risks.mitigation: Incorporate a physical home reference switch to re-zero position on each cycle, or add an absolute magnetic encoder on the output shaft.

risks.description: IP66 ingress or internal condensation at rotating/tilting dynamic mechanical joints.
risks.mitigation: Use rotary lip/labyrinth seals with drip paths, avoid rotary electrical joints, and fit a Gore-Tex pressure breather vent.

risks.description: Li-ion battery failure or hazard due to outdoor cold-temperature charging.
risks.mitigation: Implement hardware charge-inhibit below 0 °C with thermal monitoring or specify LiFePO4 cell chemistry.

tradeoffs.option: Pan Limits (Flex Wire Loop) vs. Endless Rotation (Slip Ring)
tradeoffs.benefit: Eliminates electromechanical wear part, reduces cost, simplifies IP66 sealing, preserves power/signal integrity.
tradeoffs.drawback: Cannot continuously track a target past 360° without an unwind maneuver.

tradeoffs.benefit: Reduces daily energy consumption by >80%, enabling solar/battery feasibility on umbrella mount.
tradeoffs.drawback: Does not provide continuous unbroken video recording.

tradeoffs.option: Open-Loop Stepper + Home Switch vs. Closed-Loop BLDC Servo
tradeoffs.benefit: Lower BOM cost and simpler motor control firmware.
tradeoffs.drawback: Susceptible to step skipping under wind gusts between home re-zeroing cycles.

tradeoffs.option: Shared Core with Two Variants vs. Single Universal BOM for Umbrella & Fixed-Pole PoE
tradeoffs.benefit: Optimizes power, sealing, and cost for solar umbrella without restricting performance on fixed-pole mains/PoE version.
tradeoffs.drawback: Requires maintaining two distinct product variants and SKU configurations.

evidence.claim: Standby power of ~0.3 W over 24 h equals ~7.2 Wh/day, dominating daily power consumption.
Continuous 360° pan with cabled camera causes cable fatigue and wire snapping unless bounded or passed through a slip ring.
Charging standard Li-ion cells below 0 °C causes permanent lithium plating and capacity degradation.
Patio umbrella mount is a flexible, wind-loaded structure that magnifies optical zoom motion.
Panel Wp, deployment sun-hours, battery capacity (Wh), and autonomy target days are unprovided project inputs.

next_actions: Engineer to supply solar panel rated peak power (Wp), deployment latitude / solar irradiance profile, battery capacity (Wh), and target autonomy days.
Engineer to confirm pan coverage scope: true endless 360° vs wide-coverage bounded pan limits (e.g. ±180° or ±270°).
Engineer to specify target optical zoom ratio (e.g., 3x vs 10x) and maximum operating wind speed.
Engineer to decide battery chemistry (Li-ion with low-temp charge gate vs LiFePO4).
Perform physical mount resonance sweep and zoom-in-wind stability testing to establish capped zoom ratio limit.
freeze_blockers: Unproven solar energy feasibility: solar panel Wp, deployment sun-hours, battery Wh, and target autonomy days are missing, preventing daily energy budget closure.
Unresolved pan scope decision (endless rotation vs pan limits) gating slip ring selection, cable routing, and dynamic IP66 seal design.
Unverified optical zoom usability on wind-loaded umbrella structure; maximum zoom ratio cap not yet defined through physical vibration and EIS testing.
